passage:
In history class, students studied a famous ancient library that had been damaged and lost over time. They imagined shelves of knowledge disappearing.
The teacher asked them what libraries protect today: books, digital files, local records, photos, and public access to information.
Students discussed backups, fire safety, and digital preservation.
The ancient loss felt less distant. Modern societies also risk losing knowledge through disasters, neglect, war, or technology changes.
A library is not just a building with shelves. It is a promise that memory will be cared for.
When knowledge burns or vanishes, future people lose questions they might have asked.
